claim.quote: These events have an abnormally high fraction of muons, which is beyond current model predictions.

date.note: arXiv v1 date; published in Bull. Rus. Acad. Sci. Phys. 89 (6), 894 (2025).

name: The two most powerful showers recorded by the Yakutsk array
notes: Anomaly, not a discovery: the authors raise the exotic-primary possibility without claiming it.

official_url.quote: Giant Atmospheric Showers Detected by the Yakutsk Extensive Air Shower Array

summary.plain: Of everything the Yakutsk array recorded between 1974 and 2024, two showers of about 10^20 eV were the most powerful. Both contained far more muons than current models predict, which the authors say could change our picture of hadron interactions or point to exotic primaries.
summary.technical: Two extensive air showers of about 10^20 eV registered at the Yakutsk array in 1974-2024, both near the array centre and triggering all surface and underground muon detectors (threshold 1.0 cos(theta) GeV), with an abnormally high muon fraction beyond model predictions.

title: Giant Atmospheric Showers Detected by the Yakutsk Extensive Air Shower Array
why_it_matters: The abstract says this may change our understanding of hadron interactions at ultra-high energy, but that the showers could also have been initiated by exotic primary particles.
